title: Swapping jobs with Charlie Beale to join Jimmie Noone
summary: Wilson trades places with pianist Charlie Beale to work with his idol Jimmie Noone, his last Chicago band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Chuck Beale was playing piano around Chicago, too, and Charlie Beale was playing with Jimmy Noone, and for some reason, Jimmy Noone and I swapped jobs, and I mean, Charlie Beale and I swapped jobs and it was okay with Jimmie and it was okay with Armstrong. So Charlie Beale went with Armstrong, and I went with Jimmie Noone; but Jimmie Noone was another one of my idols, too.
Before I'd ever met him, you know, as I said, I heard him in Chicago, I knew his record, the way he played 'Sweet Lorraine', and of course Earl Hines used to play with him, too.
Right, and Zinky Cohn also, later.
That's when I first heard live, Jimmie Noone, when Zinky was the piano player. So it was a privilege

for me to work with Jimmie Noone, and that'd be the last band I worked with in Chicago, and then from the Jimmie Noone band, I went to New York to play for Benny Carter. Benny Carter came out to Chicago.
